summary: Re: Security Report 01: User Enumeration via REST API Bypass on expoplatform.com

ai.s: Addressed a reported WordPress REST API user-enumeration issue on the expoplatform.com marketing site that exposed user details.
ai.pr: A security researcher reported that /wp-json/wp/v2/users/ on expoplatform.com could be accessed despite restrictions, exposing user IDs, usernames and display names.
ai.wy: Security: exposed usernames enable brute-force, privacy and phishing risks on the public website.
ai.oc: The reported user-enumeration vulnerability was tracked for mitigation, such as restricting unauthenticated access to the users endpoint.

summary: Extend Manual City Creation Validation to Include Region

ai.s: Manual City creation in the Country Manager now checks uniqueness on City, Region and Country, blocking true duplicates while allowing same-named cities elsewhere.
ai.pr: City uniqueness was checked on City and Country only, so records were created inconsistently and same-named cities in different regions were not handled correctly.
ai.wy: Consistent City records in the Country Manager across events.
ai.oc: A case-insensitive City + Region + Country uniqueness rule with a clear validation error for exact duplicates, allowing the same name in other regions or countries.

summary: Move Force Update Logic to Backend

ai.s: Force updates for the mobile app are controlled from the backend, so critical fixes can be enforced during live events without waiting on App Store timelines.
ai.pr: Force updates depended on App Store release timelines, so users could run outdated app versions during live events, as highlighted by recent incidents such as Hyve.
ai.wy: Delayed updates hurt the live event experience and strain client relationships.
ai.oc: Backend-configured version rules that the app checks on launch to enforce mandatory updates when required.

summary: Client Manager: Organizer can send Event emails with a default no-reply reply address

ai.s: Event emails now default to a no-reply Reply-To address so attendees do not reply unless the organiser explicitly allows it.
ai.pr: Registration, marketing and meeting reminder emails did not default to a no-reply Reply-To, so attendee replies could arrive unintentionally.
ai.wy: Give organisers control over whether attendees can reply to event emails.
ai.oc: Registration, marketing and meeting reminder emails use a default no-reply Reply-To address; attendee-facing content is unchanged.

summary: [TechDept] The frontend needs access to data for fields with conditional logic before any user interaction

ai.s: The Exhibitor Manual frontend receives conditional field keys and default values upfront, so conditional sections show or hide correctly on first render.
ai.pr: The backend sent conditional field data only after a user interacted with the field and saved, so the frontend could not decide which conditional sections to show initially.
ai.wy: Tech debt: admin-configured default values and checkbox conditions must apply before any interaction.
ai.oc: The sections response exposes conditional field keys and their default values before any user interaction.

summary: [Client Manager][BE FE QA] New Client Manager / Splitted to Tasks

ai.s: TAMs create customer environments, assign TAM, Sales and API teams and submit them for Finance approval in the redesigned Client Manager.
ai.pr: Client onboarding was siloed across TAMs, Finance and organisers, with no single system to create environments, assign internal teams and request approval.
ai.wy: First step of the Onboarding Journey, connecting previously siloed teams in one system.
ai.oc: A Customers Environments screen with status tabs, search and actions, a three-step Add New Customer flow, rejection resubmission, Team Members and Settings pages.

ai.s: The Organizer team defined availability and latency SLOs for the endpoints it owns, giving measurable reliability targets for its part of the platform.
ai.pr: Endpoints owned by the Organizer team had no documented, measurable reliability targets, so service-level health was not visible.
ai.wy: Engineering-wide initiative for each team to establish SLOs and gain full visibility of platform health at service level.
ai.oc: An inventory of Organizer team endpoints with availability and latency SLOs, based on Grafana data and documented in Confluence using the SLO template.

ai.s: TAMs create events for approved clients through a two-step flow with live preview and module selection, then invite an organiser admin to onboarding.
ai.pr: Once a client environment was approved, TAMs had no guided way to create customer events and trigger organiser onboarding from the admin portal.
ai.wy: Part of the TAM Onboarding journey and the Event Manager epic.
ai.oc: A two-step event creation form (general information, modules) with live preview, unsaved-changes handling, an Event created modal to add and invite admins, and an Onboarding status column.

summary: iOS/ Improve Login Flow UX When App Is Backgrounded or Device Sleeps

ai.s: iOS login keeps its progress when the app is backgrounded or the device sleeps, instead of restarting the long data load.
ai.pr: Login involved lengthy data loading; if the app was backgrounded or the device slept, the loading restarted from the beginning, increasing wait time and frustration.
ai.wy: Improve the attendee login experience in the iOS app.
ai.oc: An improved iOS login flow that handles backgrounding and sleep without restarting data loading; the story is on hold.
